gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AVS tier is a draw of about 52 W on one port (17.4 V × 3 A). So a 100 W AVS charger such as the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 drops the phone to a 45 W port as soon as a second device is plugged in. The results also do not say that the 5-port UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W (X774) passed ChargerLAB's AVS test but fell back to fixed PD in Charge-Test's test.
standout_why: Pages compared: Apple Support 102574, Charge-Test's Pro Max test, both ChargerLAB reviews (Pro and Pro Max) and iThinkDifferent. Charge-Test gives the 17.4 V/3 A request and the X774 failure. ChargerLAB gives about 52 W for an unnamed 'UGREEN 160W'. No page puts the two X774 results side by side. No page compares a multi-port AVS charger's two-device split with the 52 W the phone needs. iThinkDifferent lists the AH22 and the ESR Xtend as AVS picks but gives no AVS range and no per-port figure. Its only note on the AH22 is that 'intelligent power allocation spreads output'. LTT Labs returned 403, so I could not check it.
decides: The finding confirms single-port AVS chargers as the safe picks: the Apple 40W Dynamic and the UGREEN Nexode Air 65W (AVS version). The Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 is a confirmed AVS pick only when the phone is the only device plugged in, because with two devices each port drops to 45 W, below the 52 W tier. The UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-port (X774), which we list, should not be featured as an AVS pick because two named testers disagree. The ESR Xtend 45W stays out of the top three: its maker states only 'dynamic 45–60W' with no AVS range and no per-port figure, and no tester has confirmed AVS.
